key_points.point: The document argues that AI research and development (R&D) is a critical tool for addressing humanity's most significant challenges. By improving social good through technological progress, AI can serve as a catalyst for global advancement. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of using AI to solve grand challenges and create widespread abundance.
key_points.verbatim: Continual progress in AI research and development (R&D) can help tackle humanity’s most signiﬁcant challenges to improve social good.

key_points.point: The authors emphasize that the US plays a leading role in AI R&D, which shapes global trends. They advocate for forward-looking research policies to ensure continued progress and avoid setbacks. This supports the accelerationist view that strategic leadership in AI is vital for global progress.
key_points.verbatim: The United States (US) has kept its leading role in R&D, mainly shaping the global trends in the ﬁeld.

key_points.point: The document highlights the importance of long-term, high-risk research investments that may have large payoffs. It argues that federal investment should focus on areas where the industry is unlikely to act alone. This aligns with the accelerationist method of prioritizing foundational research to drive future capabilities.
key_points.verbatim: In addition to the incremental research with predictable short-term outcomes, this strategy aims to sustain long-term research that may be riskier but potentially have very large payoffs.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges the critical role of hardware specialized for AI and AI for improving hardware design. It recognizes that theoretical limitations of AI are tied to available hardware. This supports the accelerationist belief that compute and hardware are primary drivers of AI intelligence.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy explicitly highlights (i) knowledge discovery from multi-modal, noisy, and big data; ... (iii) understanding of theoretical limitations of AI concerning available hardware; ... (viii) hardware specialized for AI; and (ix) AI for improving hardware design.

key_points.point: The document supports the development of human-AI collaboration, noting that many applications will not be fully autonomous. It advocates for techniques that enhance human capabilities. This aligns with the accelerationist method of using AI as a super-assistant to augment human productivity.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy suggests that many applications of AI will not be completely autonomous. Instead, a combination of AI and human systems will work together.

key_points.point: The authors note the dramatic increase in funding for AI research and commercial ventures in the new millennium. They view this investment as a driver of progress. This supports the accelerationist view that capital investment is a fundamental engine for AI advancement.
key_points.verbatim: Recent years have seen a dramatic increase in the funding for AI research and commercial ventures.

key_points.label: AI as a Public Utility
key_points.point: The document highlights the importance of shared public datasets and open-source software to make AI technologies more accessible. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of democratizing access to AI resources to foster collective benefit.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy presents three critical areas of importance: ... (iii) open-source software for making AI technologies more accessible.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for public-private partnerships to leverage resources and push innovation. It argues that collaboration between government, universities, and industry is key to accelerating advances. This supports the accelerationist method of using strategic partnerships to win the race for AI development.
key_points.verbatim: The benefits of such collaboration include leveraging resources to push innovation, supporting the practices based on these innovations, and enhancing the training for future researchers and practitioners.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the US should maintain its leading role in R&D to shape global trends. This implies that national leadership is a strategic necessity for guiding the future of AI. This aligns with the accelerationist method of prioritizing national competitive advantage.
key_points.verbatim: The United States (US) has kept its leading role in R&D, mainly shaping the global trends in the ﬁeld.

key_points.point: The document argues that careful design of forward-looking research policies is crucial to avoid potential future setbacks in AI research and use. It emphasizes the need for trustworthy and safe AI. This aligns with the safetyist goal of ensuring AI is safe before it is widely deployed.
key_points.verbatim: The authors of this paper suggest that the careful design of forward-looking research policies serves a crucial function in avoiding potential future setbacks in AI research, development, and use.

key_points.point: The document calls for research into AI techniques that can explain themselves. This aligns with the safetyist method of requiring transparency and interpretability to ensure AI systems are safe and trustworthy.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy highlights some development challenges: ... (ii) AI techniques that enhance human capabilities, for instance, through wearable devices; ... (iv) human-like AI that can learn from small sample sizes, and that can explain itself.

key_points.point: The authors recommend research into monitoring and oversight mechanisms for human-AI collaboration. This aligns with the safetyist method of using AI to watch AI and ensuring human oversight in high-risk situations.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The Plan should support research initiatives that tackle questions related to understanding and improving when and how humans can oversee and modify the decisions by AI systems.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for verification and validation of AI systems to meet formal specifications. This aligns with the safetyist method of requiring rigorous testing and proof of safety before deployment.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy presents several challenges: ... (iii) enhancing verification and validation of AI systems by meeting formal specifications and user’s operational needs, respectively.

key_points.point: The authors suggest that risk ratings, certifications, and insurance are necessary mechanisms for AI systems, given that perfect safety is unattainable. This aligns with the safetyist method of using structured risk management to mitigate potential harm.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The Plan should support research initiatives that tackle questions related to understanding and operationalizing the risks and harms of AI systems so that risk ratings, certifications, and insurance become feasible for AI systems.

key_points.point: The document calls for developing standards and benchmarks for evaluating AI compliance. This aligns with the safetyist method of using standardized testing to ensure AI systems meet safety requirements.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy highlights several areas as needing further progress: ... (ii) establishing benchmarks for evaluating AI and its compliance to the standards.

key_points.point: The authors note that AI research has historically been prone to overpromising and under-delivering, leading to setbacks. This aligns with the safetyist concern that current AI progress might be overestimated, necessitating caution.
key_points.verbatim: However, the AI researchers overpromised, and the challenges were underestimated. Eventually, the promises were undelivered.

key_points.point: The document suggests that international collaboration is necessary to address the societal implications of AI. This aligns with the safetyist method of global coordination to manage AI risks.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The eighth strategy should be expanded to include collaboration with civil society organizations, particularly concerning future developments regarding the societal implications of AI.

key_points.point: The authors advocate for self-monitoring architectures for self-modifying systems. This aligns with the safetyist method of building internal safety mechanisms into AI systems.
key_points.verbatim: The strategy presents several challenges: ... (v) developing self-monitoring architectures for the safety of self-modifying systems.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need to address fairness, transparency, and accountability in AI design. This aligns with the skeptic goal of fixing AI's built-in biases to prevent discriminatory outcomes.
key_points.verbatim: This strategy focuses on fundamental concepts such as trustworthiness, fairness, transparency, accountability, explainability, and ethics.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the Plan should include social scientists from various disciplines to conduct interdisciplinary research on AI's societal implications. This aligns with the skeptic method of prioritizing social and human-centric impacts over purely technical ones.
key_points.verbatim: Accordingly, there is a growing need for social scientists with backgrounds in anthropology, economics, education, law, linguistics, political science, psychology, and sociology to conduct interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research on the challenging problems at the crossroads of AI and social sciences.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that there are studies highlighting the potential risks of AI, including unjustified optimism. This aligns with the skeptic view that AI's impact is not purely positive and requires critical assessment.
key_points.verbatim: While there are favorable views regarding the social good that AI can provide, there are also studies that criticize the unjustified and hurried optimism regarding AI for social good as well as studies that highlight the potential risks of AI.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the Plan should be strengthened to include civil society organizations. This aligns with the skeptic method of ensuring that those affected by AI have a voice in its governance.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The eighth strategy should be expanded to include collaboration with civil society organizations, particularly concerning future developments regarding the societal implications of AI.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes that AI research should aim to improve social good and keep progress at the center. This aligns with the skeptic goal of using technology for people rather than just profit.
key_points.verbatim: In this way, humans and accountable AI systems can collaborate to address society’s most significant challenges, keeping the social good and progress at the center.

key_points.point: The authors suggest that the third strategy should be rewritten to clearly present challenges concerning social implications and accountability. This aligns with the skeptic method of demanding transparency and accountability for AI's societal impacts.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The third strategy may be rewritten to present notions and challenges concerning social implications and accountability of AI systems, which include concepts such as responsibility, explainability, robustness, and fairness.

key_points.point: The document notes that commercial vendors in the past failed to develop workable solutions for real-world problems, leading to the second AI Winter. This aligns with the skeptic view that AI's commercial promises often exceed its actual capabilities.
key_points.verbatim: However, commercial vendors failed to develop workable solutions for real-world problems.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the Plan should include Causal AI as a research area. This aligns with the skeptic method of seeking deeper understanding of AI systems to ensure they are not just pattern-matching tools.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The Plan should include Causal AI and the integration between symbolic and connectionist approaches as additional areas that require commitment for long-term fundamental research.

key_points.point: The document calls for research into how humans can oversee and modify AI decisions. This aligns with the skeptic method of maintaining human control and accountability over AI systems.
key_points.verbatim: Recommendation: The Plan should support research initiatives that tackle questions related to understanding and improving when and how humans can oversee and modify the decisions by AI systems.

factual_claims.claim: The Dartmouth workshop in 1956 is widely considered the founding event of AI as a research field.
The US spent over 600 billion dollars on gross domestic R&D in 2019.
The first version of the National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan was published in 2016.
The National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan was updated in 2019.
The first neural net machine was created in 1951.
The Logic Theorist program, capable of proving mathematical theorems, was developed in 1956.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A cross-cutting concept that advocates for integrating knowledge from various disciplines, such as social sciences and humanities, into AI research to address complex societal challenges. It emphasizes the need to cross disciplinary boundaries.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The authors argue that multidisciplinary teams are insufficient and that an interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approach is needed to integrate knowledge from various disciplines to cross disciplinary boundaries.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept highlights the need for a broader research base for AI, which is currently not explicitly represented in the taxonomy.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Interdisciplinary research can help identify new, innovative applications for AI by bringing in diverse domain expertise.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Interdisciplinary research is crucial for understanding the complex, emergent risks of AI and developing robust alignment and control mechanisms.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptical Interpretation: Interdisciplinary research is necessary to ensure that AI development is informed by social and ethical considerations, preventing the perpetuation of existing biases and harms.
